summary.title: Don't Do This
summary.one_liner: A PostgreSQL wiki checklist of common mistakes to avoid, with the reasons why and the rare cases where each practice is acceptable.
takeaways: Avoid NOT IN with possible NULLs and prefer NOT EXISTS, which also plans better as an anti-join.
Store points in time as timestamptz, and avoid timestamp(0), timetz, and CURRENT_TIME.
Use text with a CHECK constraint instead of char(n), and prefer text or varchar over varchar(n) by default.
Never use trust authentication over TCP/IP in production; use scram-sha-256 or peer auth instead.
Use triggers rather than rules, native partitioning rather than table inheritance, and identity columns rather than serial on PostgreSQL 10+.
summary.summary: This wiki page lists common PostgreSQL mistakes across encoding, tooling, SQL constructs, date/time types, text types, other data types, and authentication. Each entry follows the same pattern: the recommendation, a "Why not?" explanation, and a "When should you?" section describing the rare exceptions. It cites examples and manual passages, such as NULL behavior in NOT IN, BETWEEN's closed interval, and the padding behavior of char(n). It also mentions the schemalint tool for checking a schema against these recommendations.
